summary: Two correctness issues affect this script. Most urgently, its final `display` command is syntactically invalid, so the accumulated statistics are not printed. The comparison predicates also treat mutually blank components as agreement, which can inflate whole-name agreement categories when partial/blank transcriptions exist.

findings.title: The final display command treats result values as invalid options
findings.what_the_code_does: After macro expansion, `noisily di `denom', `numer1', ...` becomes a command such as `display 100, 20, 30...`. In Stata, text after the first comma is parsed as display options, not additional expressions.
findings.why_it_matters: The command errors rather than emitting the denominator and four category counts—the sole output of this script—so the requested comparison result is not produced.
findings.how_to_check: Run the do-file, or run `display 100, 20` in Stata; it should return a syntax/invalid-option error.
findings.suggested_fix: Display a single formatted string, for example: `noisily di "denom=`denom' ancestry_only=`numer1' fs_only=`numer2' both=`numer3' neither=`numer4'"`.

findings.title: Whole-name agreement counts shared blank first or last names as matches
findings.what_the_code_does: Eligibility requires only one nonempty field per commercial source, but each category then uses componentwise equality. Thus, for example, `namefrst==namefrst_ml` is true when both are `""`; a surname-only record can therefore be classified as a full-name match based solely on the surname.
findings.why_it_matters: This can inflate the ‘Ancestry only,’ ‘FamilySearch only,’ and ‘both’ counts, and changes their interpretation from agreement on a complete two-field name to agreement on whichever field happens to be populated.
findings.how_to_check: Within each `merged_data.dta`, tabulate the four categories separately for observations where any compared component is blank; e.g., count eligible records with `namefrst=="" | fs_namefrst=="" | namefrst_ml=="" | namelast=="" | fs_namelast=="" | namelast_ml_ditto==""`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either restrict a whole-name comparison to nonempty first and surname fields for all relevant sources/model outputs, or calculate and report first-name and surname agreement separately for partial-name records.

verified_clean.item: The four comparison categories partition the stated eligible sample.
verified_clean.evidence: CODE/comparing_model_transcription_with_anc_fs_SSHA2025.do:43, CODE/comparing_model_transcription_with_anc_fs_SSHA2025.do:47, CODE/comparing_model_transcription_with_anc_fs_SSHA2025.do:51, and CODE/comparing_model_transcription_with_anc_fs_SSHA2025.do:55 implement respectively A-not-F, F-not-A, A-and-F, and neither; these are mutually exclusive and exhaustive conditional on line 39.

verified_clean.item: State-level totals are initialized before the loop and accumulated immediately after each `count`.

review_limits: I reviewed source only; the state-level data and Stata runtime were unavailable.
I could not determine the prevalence or intended treatment of partial/blank names, so the magnitude of blank-string inflation is unverified.
I did not assess claims, identification, or replication dimensions because the request scoped this review to correctness.
